chunks: By Allah, if I had refused it, its obligation would not have been incumbent upon me, nor would Allah have burdened me with its sin,
and by Allah, now that I have accepted it, I am the rightful one who should be followed, and certainly the Book is with me; I have not forsaken it since I kept company with it.
For we were with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and killing revolved among fathers, sons, brothers, and relatives,
so we did not increase in every calamity and hardship except in faith, and perseverance upon the truth, and submission to the command, and patience with the pain of wounds.
ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali justify his acceptance of arbitration to the Kharijites in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) clarifies that his acceptance of arbitration was a pragmatic political decision rather than a divine obligation, asserting his authority as the 'rightful one to be followed.' He contextualizes this within the shared trials of the Prophet's household, emphasizing that enduring the 'bitterness of wounds' in battle only deepened their faith and submission to God's command. This reflects the Shia scholarly view of *sabr* (patience) not as passive resignation, but as active perseverance in truth amidst political turmoil.

en.sayed-ali-raza: By Allāh, if I had refused it, it would not have been obligatory on me. Nor would Allāh have laid its sin on me.
And by Allāh, now that I have accepted it, I alone am the rightful person who should be followed, for certainly the Qur’ān is with me. I never forsake it since I adopted its company.
We have been with the Prophet in battles wherein those killed were fathers, sons, brothers and relations of one another.
Nevertheless, every trouble and hardship just increased us in our belief, in our treading on the right path, in submission to (divine) command and in endurance of the pain of wounds.
